clue.text: Nasty lunch oozes egg — oral medication required?

indicators.note: something nasty has been spoiled or mangled, so the letters that follow are scrambled

parts.note: all thirteen letters of the three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A revolting meal of oozing egg seems to demand something to settle the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Cough lozenges are sweets sucked in the mouth to soothe the throat, a medicine taken orally.

clue.text: Exclaim about a bit of medicine and a blood vessel

indicators.note: one word goes round the others, wrapping about them

parts.note: to exclaim is to cry out
a pill is a single dose of medicine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone yelps at a dose of medicine and a vein.
explanation.walkthrough: CRY splits after its first letter to hold A PILL and A together, giving CAPILLARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A capillary is one of the tiny vessels carrying blood between arteries and veins.

clue.text: Idiot blocking American military groups?

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: standard abbreviation
nit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A fool obstructs US armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that units need not be military; nit is mild British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Units are organised bodies within an army, such as battalions or companies.

clue.text: Information about health centre, perhaps — it's very light

indicators.note: information about something is placed beside the subject it concerns, so the two parts are simply joined

parts.note: a hydro is a British hotel or spa offering water cures; 'perhaps' marks it as an example
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Details about a health spa are offered with a remark about how little something weighs.
explanation.walkthrough: The information comes second: HYDRO then GEN. A hydro is a spa hotel, and gen is informal British for the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen is the lightest chemical element, the least dense gas.

clue.text: Shellfish, ordinarily gutted, with rest cooked

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed up
a gutted word has had its insides removed, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
these four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe note: shellfish, usually cleaned out, then cooked with whatever remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is a bivalve mollusc, a common edible shellfish.

clue.text: Went overseas, largely put out and vexed

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to emit is to give out or put out
something that grated irritated or vexed

explanation.surface: Someone moved abroad, mostly because they were annoyed and irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to settle in another, so the person went abroad.

clue.text: Sports grand titles, after declining first one

indicators.note: declining means refusing, so the opening letter is turned away
one piece comes after the other, so they are placed in sequence

parts.note: G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand
a title is a name

explanation.surface: Grand sporting championships, with the first one turning someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: Games are sporting contests, as in the Olympic Games, so the plural noun matches sports.

clue.text: Almost certain aspect will be lacking depth

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: sure means certain
a face is one aspect or side of something

explanation.surface: A near-certain feature of something is that it will be shallow.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, surface means superficial, involving only the outward appearance rather than anything deeper.

clue.text: Mother's extra heart is a concern

indicators.note: the possessive makes the next piece belong to, and sit inside, the word for mother

parts.note: mater is Latin for mother, an old public-school word

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the middle letter of the five

explanation.surface: Mum's additional worry is a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter is a subject of concern, as in a matter for the police.

clue.text: Computer package misled regarding purpose

parts.note: an app is a software application
someone who lied misled others

explanation.surface: A piece of software gave false information about what it is for.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied, as in applied science, describes knowledge put to practical use rather than pursued for itself.

clue.text: Olympic athlete to seem angry about weight

indicators.note: one word goes round the other, about it

parts.note: to simmer is to seethe with suppressed anger
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: An Olympian appears furious about their weigh-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer competes in the pool events, one kind of athlete at the Olympic Games.

clue.text: The French policeman needed in support? Shut up

indicators.note: what is needed in something has to go inside it

parts.note: a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball
les is French for the (plural)
a cop is a police officer

explanation.surface: A French officer is called in to help, and told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' is not a demand for silence but a verb meaning to close by collapsing.
explanation.definitionFit: To telescope is to collapse in sections, like a folding telescope, so it closes or shuts up.

clue.text: Some Emperor a star? That's what I believe

definitions.note: the answer is the believer who would say this, not the belief

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of them, a run of letters taken from inside

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the next two

explanation.surface: Someone affirms faith that an emperor is a star.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: Rastafarians revere the Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta is a follower of Rastafarianism, which holds the Ethiopian emperor divine, so this is the believer speaking.

clue.text: Car list including promotional item

indicators.note: one word including another holds it inside

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties or names
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A motor catalogue features an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadster is an open two-seater sports car.

clue.text: "Speed in it's elevated": the writer, describing Einstein's continuum

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other
in a down entry, raising letters means reading them from the bottom up

parts.note: the letters, apostrophe dropped
pace means speed
the writer refers to herself or himself as me

explanation.surface: A writer quotes a phrase about speed being raised while explaining relativity.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacetime is the four-dimensional continuum of relativity theory, joining three space dimensions with time.

clue.text: Attack from the air? Airmen in difficult position, mostly

indicators.note: the airmen are placed in the other word
mostly means all but a bit, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to be in a stew is to be in trouble
the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: Pilots in a tight spot launch an air raid.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Scholar I made out, engaged in dubious acts

indicators.note: something engaged in an activity is inside it
worked out means rearranged into a solution
something dubious is not straight, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: these letters reordered
these letters reordered

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to inventing things while involved in shady dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: An academist is an academic, a member of an academy or learned society.

clue.text: One engaged in theft, if unfortunate, will get 2%

indicators.note: something engaged in an activity is inside it
an unfortunate state of affairs has gone awry, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thief, if unlucky, gets a two per cent share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One engaged in theft' reads as a thief, but it is an instruction to put a letter inside the word theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Two per cent is two hundredths, which is the same as one fiftieth.

clue.text: Wait for routine song

parts.note: a way of doing things is a routine
a lay is an old word for a ballad or song

explanation.surface: Someone waits for a familiar tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To waylay is to lie in wait for someone in order to intercept or ambush them.

clue.text: We will get protective gear, seeing off latest in nuclear munitions

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: seeing something off gets rid of it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: aprons protect clothing

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its last one

parts.note: the final letter, the one taken out

explanation.surface: We will be issued protective clothing, getting rid of nuclear arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons are arms; munitions is a general word for military weapons and ammunition.

clue.text: Twist has dependent child facing a blow

parts.note: to wind is to twist or coil
a ward is a child in someone's legal care

explanation.surface: Oliver Twist, the orphan, is braced for a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' looks like Dickens's orphan, which suits 'dependent child', but here it means to coil. The blow is a wind, not a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Windward is the side facing into the wind, so it faces the blowing air.

clue.text: Be exhaustive about rear end of old English dog

indicators.note: the rear end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter
standard abbreviation
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: Someone goes on at length about the back end of an old English dog breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' reads as a noun but works as the verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail something is to describe it item by item, covering it thoroughly.

clue.text: That chap, beset by excess weight, taking up interest

indicators.note: in a down entry, taking letters up means reading them from the bottom up
something beset by another is surrounded by it

parts.note: flab is excess body fat
a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man surrounded by fat takes up a new hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: Behalf means interest or benefit, as in acting on someone's behalf, in their interest.

clue.text: A regret, without good reason

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
to rue is to regret
G for good

explanation.surface: Someone expresses remorse for no good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside: RUE sits outside G, making ARGUE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to reason, to present a case with logical points.

clue.text: Governor about to swallow a fruit

indicators.note: what swallows something takes it inside

parts.note: guv is British slang for a boss or governor
a. is an abbreviation for about, as with circa
taken as written

explanation.surface: The boss is on the verge of gulping down a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the verge of'; it is the abbreviation A, and GUV with A then takes in the other A.
explanation.definitionFit: A guava is a tropical fruit with pink or white flesh.

clue.text: Run to forestall missing a lively character?

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: to avert is to forestall or prevent
the letter removed

explanation.surface: A dash to stop someone missing out on a vivacious person.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravert, also spelt extrovert, is an outgoing, sociable person, typically lively company.

clue.text: Field of operation's area around the kidneys? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so the last letter goes

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
renal means relating to the kidneys

explanation.surface: A surgeon's working zone is the region round the kidneys, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a sphere of activity, a place or field where something is carried on.

clue.text: Runs a company, back in America, producing wind instrument

indicators.note: going back means the letters run the other way

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written
standard abbreviation
taken as written
A is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: Someone running a firm back in the States makes musical instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped flute, a wind instrument blown through a mouthpiece.

clue.text: Recalled fifth article about Royal Institution's distinguished fellows

parts.note: E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: one word goes round the other, about it
called back, so the letters are read in the opposite order

parts.note: an item is an article
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A fifth paper is withdrawn about the Royal Institution's eminent members.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are retired professors who keep their honorary title, plural of emeritus.

clue.text: Foretaste that has development around electronic current technology

indicators.note: development changes how something is arranged, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: all thirteen letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: An early taste of new electronics hints at the latest gadgetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words supply every letter; 'around' is only a loose link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: State of the art describes the most advanced, up-to-date version of a technology.
